status_label: Completed & Verified — Phase 2 Official HuggingFace Weights & Software-vs-RTL Comparison Published

reviewer_decisions.reason:
Approve Phase 2 engineering delivery for the authoritative official-checkpoint slice. The implementation parses and validates the raw safetensors data, preserves packed words and binary16 memory responses, and separates raw-F16-derived FP32 arithmetic from the fixed-point oracle. The documented two-layer fixture maps logical layers 0/1 to official layers 0/23 without manufactured weights. This satisfies the explicit bounded-slice rule; it does not claim full 24-layer inference.

I read tests/official_weights.py, the verification entry point and public-pin transactors, relevant RTL, generated simulation assertions, retained failure diagnostics, and recorded results. The standalone sweep completes all 14 official 64×64 submatrices: 57,344 products and 896 compared writes. The top-level simulation completes two prefill and two decode tokens, using IDs 0, 1, 59, 59, with 6,144 ordered scratch/cache writes and 256 logits compared against the integer oracle, with zero bit mismatches. evidence/verification/functional/official-slice-top-simulate.stdout records final-logit transfers and retirement for all four tokens, 276,557 aggregate token-latency cycles, and 90,952 acknowledged memory transactions. The comparison file records cosine similarity 0.9999992996, MAE 0.0007060303, RMSE 0.0008419820, maximum absolute error 0.0018793344, and complete top-1/top-5 agreement. Both requested comparison paths are present.

The recorded behavior, sensitivity, synthesis and portability commands completed successfully. Their inspected implementations retain the A/B/C/D seeded regressions and numerical limits, require intended functional assertions for mutation detection, perform actual Yosys lowering and zero-latch/connectivity checks, and exercise matched Icarus 12/13 compilation and public-protocol simulation. The earlier literal-layer harness failure remains in evidence/preparation/verifier-phase2-raw-integration-02; the corrected check distinguishes layer-zero scratch addresses from physical-layer model addresses. Missing full-checkpoint coordinates remain an exercised negative test, not a blocker for the authorized slice. These results establish simulated RTL correctness and measured slice accuracy/latency, not silicon throughput or physical sign-off. I executed no commands and changed no files.
